data.name: Sample - Fortinet FortiSIEM v2 - 6.0.4
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "Fortinet FortiSIEM v2" connector. If you are planning to use any of the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

arguments.last_pull_time: {% if not vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'] or vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'][0].value == '0' or vars.request.env_setup %}{{ arrow.utcnow().shift(minutes=-(vars.minutes | int)).format('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss') }}Z{% else %}{{ vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'][0].value }}{% endif %}

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Wizard-editable defaults. `minutes` is the cold-start lookback used the
first time this ingestion runs (macro still '0'); after that the macro
supplies the window. The macro name is scoped to this playbook's UUID so
two ingestion configurations never share a watermark.

groups.name: Note: Environment Setup
groups.description:
Runs when the watermark macro does not exist yet -- not only on the
wizard's `vars.request.env_setup` first pass.

Keying solely off env_setup left ingestion permanently broken whenever
the macro was missing: `Update Last Alert Pull Time` only *updates*, it
does not create, so every run cold-started at `minutes` and the watermark
was never written. Live-verified on 8.0.0: 100 scheduled runs, all
`finished`, zero alerts created and no macro on the appliance -- a
silent failure, because nothing errors.

This step must therefore come AFTER Get Macro Value, so its absence can
be seen. The macro is primed to '0', which Set Time Configuration reads
as "cold start" for this one run.

groups.name: Note: Set Time Configuration
groups.description:
`curr_timestamp` is captured before the fetch and only written back to
the macro after Ingest succeeds, so a failed run re-pulls its window
instead of silently skipping it.

groups.name: Note: Save Result
groups.description:
The Fetch -> Ingest contract. Ingest reads every one of these back as
`vars.result.<key>`.

workflows.name: FortiSIEM v2 > Ingest
workflows.description: Orchestrator: calls Fetch, creates the alerts, then advances the last-pull-time watermark.

arguments.alerts_type_map: {'Actionable Threat Feeds': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Actionable Threat Feeds')}}, 'Brute Force Attempts': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Brute Force Attempts')}}, 'Command and Control': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Command and Control')}}, 'Concurrent Login': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Concurrent Login')}}, 'Data Exfiltration': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Data Exfiltration')}}, 'Denial of Service': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Denial of Service')}}, 'Lateral Movement': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Lateral Movement')}}, 'MITRE ATT&CK': {{'AlertType'| picklist('MITRE ATT&CK')}}, 'Malware': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Malware')}}, 'Other / Unknown': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Other / Unknown')}}, 'Phishing': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Phishing')}}, 'Policy Violation': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Policy Violation')}}, 'Ransomware': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Ransomware')}}, 'Reconnaissance': {{'AlertType'| picklist('Reconnaissance')}}}

routes.name: Create Alerts -> Update Last Alert Pull Time

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Severity/status/type maps are keyed on the values `field_mapping.py` emits
and cover every one of them -- an unmapped value would make `resolveRange`
miss and the alert POST fail with a picklist 400. `field_mapping` clamps
alert_type to VALID_ALERT_TYPES for exactly this reason, so the two lists
have to be changed together.

groups.name: Note: Create Alerts
groups.description:
`is_upsert` routes this at /api/3/upsert/alerts, keyed on `sourceId`, so a
re-ingest updates the existing alert. Without it the plain insert path
409s on the sourceid uniqueness constraint the moment a window overlaps a
previous run -- which every incremental pull does.

groups.name: Note: Update Last Alert Pull Time
groups.description:
Advances the watermark only after the alerts are written, so a failed
Create Alerts leaves the window to be retried.
